title: One count for any mod, any version
text: The end goal is any mod to any version, forward or back (Jon, 2026-11-21: 'any version <-> any version, not necessarily the newest version or a small jump'), but the scoreboard counted one update at a time, a few jumps forward, and the most-used release to the newest; ports to older releases were not measured at all. The every-update run now also ports the 150 most-downloaded mods of each loader's most-used release (Fabric 1.20.1, NeoForge 1.21.1) to every other release the loader has, 43 and 21, back to 1.14.4 and 1.20.2, and counts the mods whose port links on every one: port.jar-links.any-version, the porting goal's headline. For each mod that misses it lists the releases and the types of break holding it there, ranked by what would free the most mods (scoreboard/any-version.md on the generated branch, written by main's run after each merge).
finish: port.jar-links.any-version is computed by tools/cloud-run exposure and by main's run after each merge (written to the generated branch with its what's-not list, scoreboard/any-version.md), first on ROADMAP.md; a first number from a cloud run of this branch, per loader, with the top blockers
wrongIf: a mod counted as going to any version misses a release in its own per-update summary, or a release whose job did not run is left out of the count instead of counted as not reached
result: 6 of 300 go to any version (cloud run 45160319659, every job green): Fabric 2 of 150 from 1.20.1 to all 43 other releases (fabric-language-kotlin, yosbr; 5 reach every newer one, 2 every older one back to 1.14.4), NeoForge 4 of 150 from 1.21.1 to all 21 (continuity, e4mc, fast-ip-ping, rhino; 15 every newer, 4 every older back to 1.20.2). Ports back are measured: the six were checked against every target's own summary. Top blockers: 6 mods unreadable on every release (crash-assistant, customskinloader, essential, both loaders), 3 held only by data ids a release lacks; no release alone holds a mod back. The run first failed twice on crashes the backward chains exposed: a route map reading uses with different numbers of operands, and two downloads of one library deleting each other's file; both fixed
